[[ ## identity ## ]]
You are Dana Whitfield, Controller at Kestrel Manufacturing. Precise and numbers-fluent; expects the same back. Ongoing concerns: keeping the business moving.

[[ ## situation ## ]]
From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes
Subject: Margin number for Thursday board — need your numbers

Gabriel,

I need the margin reconciliation for Q3 before Thursday’s board call. Specifically, the gross margin step-down from last quarter — the board is asking why we dropped from 34.2% to 31.8%, and I need to show them exactly where the delta sits.

Can you pull the COGS detail and any inventory adjustments that hit the close? I want the full breakdown by product line, not just the aggregate. Also flag anything unusual — freight, scrap, rework — because they’ll push on that.

Victor is on the loop so he has visibility. Get me the numbers by end of day Wednesday so I can build the explanation.

Thanks,
Dana

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Margin number for Thursday board — need your numbers

Hi Dana,

Got it — I’ll have the full Q3 margin reconciliation for you by end of day Wednesday, with the gross margin step-down from 34.2% to 31.8% broken out by product line. I’ll include the COGS detail and any inventory adjustments that hit the close, and I’ll flag anything unusual — freight, scrap, rework — as you asked, so you can build the board narrative.

I’ll also pull the prior quarter comparative so you can show the delta clearly, not just the aggregate. If anything looks off in the underlying data, I’ll call it out in a note alongside the numbers rather than burying it.

I’ll send it to you directly, and I’ll loop Victor in on the final version so he has visibility.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes

---

From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes
Subject: Re: Margin number for Thursday board — need your numbers

Gabriel,

Thanks for the quick confirmation. Just to be clear—Wednesday end-of-day is the drop-dead, not the goal. I need time to stress-test the numbers and build the bridge before Thursday morning.

One more thing: when you flag the unusual items (freight, scrap, rework), quantify them in dollars and as a percentage of the step-down. The board will ask “how much of the 240 basis points is this?”—I need to answer that without guessing.

Also, if you see any inventory adjustments that look like they're timing-related (e.g., a late receipt or a valuation change), separate those out. They’ll want to know what's permanent vs. one-time.

Send it directly to me, loop Victor on the final version as noted. If anything surfaces that changes the story—like a reclassification—tell me in the note, don’t bury it.

Dana

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Margin number for Thursday board — need your numbers

Hi Dana,

Understood — Wednesday end-of-day is the drop-dead, and I’ll have the full Q3 margin reconciliation to you well before then so you have time to stress-test and build the bridge.

To confirm scope: I’ll break out the step-down from 34.2% to 31.8% by product line, with COGS detail and any inventory adjustments that hit the close. For the unusual items — freight, scrap, rework — I’ll quantify each in dollars and as a percentage of the 240-basis-point delta, so you can answer “how much of this is X?” without guessing.

I’ll also separate timing-related inventory adjustments (late receipts, valuation changes) from permanent ones, so the board can see what’s one-time vs. structural. If anything surfaces that changes the story — reclassification or otherwise — I’ll flag it clearly in the note, not bury it.

I’ll send the final version directly to you and loop Victor in as noted.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes

---

From: Victor Alade
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Margin number for Thursday board — need your numbers

Dana,

I don't have the final reconciled numbers yet — Gabriel's delivery is still expected Wednesday EOD per your drop-dead. But I can give you the working figure based on the last close package I reviewed:

- Q3 gross margin is tracking at 31.8% (240 bps step-down from 34.2%).
- I've seen preliminary COGS detail; the biggest drivers so far are freight and scrap in two product lines, but I haven't quantified them against the delta yet.
- No reclassifications flagged in my review as of now, but that could change once Gabriel's final breakdown lands.

I'll review Gabriel's numbers the moment they hit and flag anything that changes the story before you build the bridge. If anything looks off, you'll hear from me directly.

Best,
V

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Margin number for Thursday board — need your numbers

Hi Dana,

Quick follow-up to confirm I'm still on track for the Wednesday end-of-day drop-dead on the Q3 margin reconciliation. I'm in the final pass now, and the breakdown by product line, COGS detail, and inventory adjustments are all coming together as promised.

For the unusual items — freight, scrap, rework — I've quantified each in dollars and as a percentage of the 240-basis-point step-down, so you'll have the "how much of this is X?" answer ready for the board. I've also separated timing-related inventory adjustments (late receipts, valuation changes) from permanent ones.

One thing I'm watching: there's an odd inventory line in Kestrel's June package that could look like a timing item but is actually a late vendor rebate credit rebooked per accrual policy. I'm documenting it clearly in the note so it doesn't get misread as a permanent margin issue. I'll flag it explicitly rather than let it sit buried in the numbers.

I'll send the final version directly to you and loop Victor as agreed, well before end of day tomorrow.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes

---

Subject: Working Q3 margin figure for Thursday

Dana,

While Gabriel's final reconciliation is still due Wednesday EOD, here's my working figure so you can start building the bridge:

From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes, Victor Alade
Subject: Re: Margin number for Thursday board — need your numbers

Gabriel, Victor,

Gabriel, thanks for the heads-up on the late vendor rebate credit in the June package. That's exactly the kind of thing I need called out separately — I don't want it buried in a timing line where the board might misinterpret it as a structural margin issue. Make sure the note is explicit on that point.

Victor, appreciate the working figure. I'll use the 31.8% as a placeholder but will hold off building the full bridge until Gabriel's final numbers land Wednesday EOD. Once I have the quantified breakdown — dollars and basis points per driver — I'll stress-test and finalize the board narrative.

One ask for both of you: if anything else surfaces between now and Wednesday EOD that changes the 240-basis-point story — whether it's a reclassification, a valuation adjustment, or another timing item — flag it to me immediately, not in the final package. I'd rather know early than have to rework the bridge Thursday morning.

Keep me posted if anything shifts. Otherwise, I'll expect the final from you, Gabriel, with Victor on the loop.

Dana

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Margin number for Thursday board — need your numbers

Hi Dana,

Acknowledged — I'm on track for the Wednesday end-of-day drop-dead, and I'll have the full Q3 margin reconciliation to you directly, with Victor on the loop as agreed.

To confirm the final scope: product-line breakdown of the 34.2% to 31.8% step-down, COGS detail, inventory adjustments, and dollar + basis-point quantification for freight, scrap, and rework. Timing-related items (late receipts, valuation changes) will be separated from permanent ones, and I'll flag anything that changes the story immediately — not just in the final package.

On the Kestrel June item: I'll make the note explicit that the late vendor rebate credit (~$18K) is a timing/accrual rebook, not a structural margin issue. It will be clearly separated and labeled so the board doesn't misread it.

If anything surfaces between now and Wednesday EOD that shifts the 240-basis-point picture, you'll hear from me right away. Otherwise, expect the final package by end of day Wednesday.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes
